title: Your Fingers Have Tendons Stronger Than Your Biceps
description:
Your fingers have no muscles in them at all. Everything they do is done by tendons running from your forearms. Test your finger tendons, learn the science, and train them with me.

Educational content, not medical advice. Stop if you feel pain.

#grip #tendon #calisthenics #climbing #strength

scenes.caption: DO THIS NOW
scenes.narration: Do this with me right now. Find a door frame, a ledge, anything you can hook your fingers over. Hang from just your fingertips and count the seconds. Ten seconds is normal. Twenty is strong. Thirty means your finger tendons are already better than most people's. Remember your number, because we are coming back to it.

scenes.caption: ZERO MUSCLES IN YOUR FINGERS
scenes.narration: Here is the strange fact that makes this whole video work. Your fingers have no muscles in them. None. Open your hand, close it, hold your whole body weight from a ledge. Every bit of that is done by tendons, long cables running from muscles in your forearm all the way to your fingertips. When you train grip, you are not training muscle. You are training cable.

scenes.label: OF FINGER STRENGTH IS TENDON
scenes.sub: the muscles live in the forearm - the fingers are pure cable
scenes.narration: One hundred percent. That is how much of your finger strength is tendon. And tendons are trainable, just like the Achilles we covered before, but with one difference: finger tendons are thin, they have almost no blood supply, and they adapt even slower. That is why climbers who rush finger training get injured, and why the patient ones end up with hands like steel hooks.

scenes.head: STUDY - TENDON ADAPTATION
scenes.narration: The research on tendon tissue keeps saying the same thing, and finger tendons are the purest example. Slow, heavy, still loading is what tells tendon to remodel. Not fast reps. Not maximum attempts every day. Long holds, moderate intensity, and time. So today we do not max out. We hang, we hold, and we build.
Move one. Dead hang. Full grip, straight arms, thirty seconds on, fifteen off. This loads the whole chain, fingers to shoulders. Go.
Move two. Fingertip hang. Feet on the ground if you need them, just enough weight to feel the fingers work. Twenty seconds, slow and controlled. Never bounce on the fingertips. Go.

scenes.caption: THE MISTAKE
scenes.narration: Now the mistake that ruins more finger tendons than any other. People test their hang, get ten seconds, and decide to train it every day at maximum effort, hanging until their fingers open. That is exactly backwards. Thin tendons with almost no blood supply do not recover like muscle. They need forty-eight hours between hard sessions, and they need sub-maximal holds, not failure. The climbers with the strongest fingers in the world train them two or three times a week, never to failure, and they have done it for years. Boring beats heroic, every time, for this tissue.

scenes.title: THE FINGER LADDER
layers: months later - one hand, one finger less
scenes.narration: And here is the ladder, so you know where this goes. Level one is the dead hang you just did. Level two is the fingertip hang, feet still helping you. Level three, months from now, is taking weight off one hand at a time. You do not skip levels. A tendon that was never loaded at level one will not survive level three, and it will tell you so with months of pain. The ladder is the program. Climb it one rung at a time.

scenes.caption: TEST IT EVERY MONTH
scenes.narration: One more habit that costs nothing. Test your hang once a month, same ledge, same grip, and write the number down. Tendon progress is invisible day to day and obvious month to month. If your number climbs by two seconds a month, you are winning, even if your hands look exactly the same in the mirror. The mirror shows muscle. The stopwatch shows tendon.

scenes.label: THE HONEST TIMELINE
scenes.sub: thin tendons, slow blood flow - patience is the program
scenes.narration: Ninety days. That is the honest timeline for finger tendons, maybe more than any other tissue we will cover on this channel. But the payoff is permanent. A grip built on tendon does not fade in two weeks off. It stays. Test your hang again in ninety days, and tell me your seconds in the comments. Next video, we make your punch heavier with the same science. This is Wire Strength. Train the cable.
